hook: A secret message is scrambled by multiplying blocks of numbers by a matrix. To read it, you need the matrix that undoes the scrambling. One number, the determinant, tells you whether such an undo matrix exists, and it also measures how much the matrix stretches areas.

prereq.q: What is the area of a parallelogram with base $5$ and height $3$?

figure.caption: The columns of $\left[ \begin{matrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{matrix} \right]$, drawn as $\left\langle 3, 1 \right\rangle$ and $\left\langle 1, 2 \right\rangle$, make a parallelogram of area $3(2) - 1(1) = 5$, the determinant.

chain.cause: For $A = \left[ \begin{matrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{matrix} \right]$, compute $ad - bc$
Draw the two columns of $A$ as vectors from the origin
chain.effect: they make a parallelogram whose area is $\left| \det A \right|$
$A$ has an inverse: swap $a$ and $d$, negate $b$ and $c$, divide by $\det A$
the columns lie on one line, the parallelogram is flat, and A has no inverse

ideas: The determinant of $\left[ \begin{matrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{matrix} \right]$ is $ad - bc$. Its absolute value is the area of the parallelogram made by the two columns.
The inverse matrix $A^{-1}$ satisfies $AA^{-1} = A^{-1}A = I$. For $\det A \ne 0$: $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc}\left[ \begin{matrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{matrix} \right]$.
$\det A = 0$ means no inverse: two different inputs give the same product, so nothing can undo $A$.
If $AX = B$ and $A$ has an inverse, then $X = A^{-1}B$.

misconception.wrong: The inverse of $\left[ \begin{matrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{matrix} \right]$ is $\left[ \begin{matrix} \frac{1}{a} & \frac{1}{b} \\ \frac{1}{c} & \frac{1}{d} \end{matrix} \right]$.
misconception.right: Reciprocals of the entries do not undo matrix multiplication. Swap $a$ and $d$, change the signs of $b$ and $c$, and divide by $ad - bc$; then check that $AA^{-1} = I$.

summary: For a $2 \times 2$ matrix the determinant $ad - bc$ is the signed area of the parallelogram made by its columns. If it is not $0$, the inverse is $\frac{1}{ad - bc}\left[ \begin{matrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{matrix} \right]$, which undoes the matrix and solves $AX = B$ as $X = A^{-1}B$. If it is $0$, there is no inverse.
